text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 3.6% today as crude oil prices spiked to over $105 per barrel following reports that Saudi Arabia closed a major pipeline after a drone attack. Refineries are running at near-full capacity (97.8%), which means the company benefits when oil prices rise and margins improve — they can process more barrels at higher-margin spreads between crude input costs and refined product sales.

The broader backdrop amplifies the move: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are tightening global oil supply, and analysts warn that if Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays offline beyond the next week, prices could rally even further. A refiner holding a full order book at high utilization rates stands to gain from this supply squeeze.
